title: Generics
summary: Writing type-safe code that works for any type - generic methods and classes, type inference, constraints with where (class, struct, new(), interfaces, notnull), generic interfaces, default(T), covariance in IEnumerable and IReadOnlyList, and why generics beat object.

cards.q: What does where T : IComparable<T> allow inside a generic method?
cards.a:
Calling CompareTo on values of type T

The constraint promises that every T has a `CompareTo` method, so `a.CompareTo(b)` compiles. Operators like `<` are not part of the interface.

cards.q: Why can a List<Circle> be passed as IEnumerable<Shape> but not as List<Shape>?
cards.a:
IEnumerable<T> only hands items out; a List<Shape> would let you add a square to the circles

`IEnumerable<out T>` is covariant because it is read-only. If a `List<Circle>` were a `List<Shape>`, `Add(new Square())` would put a square into a list of circles, so the conversion is not allowed even with a cast.

null

string is a reference type, so its default is null.
